resolutions.researcher_notes: Status is inferred, not a literal token (per standing guidance). Live opec.org original is dead (known batch gotcha, redirects to homepage); the Wayback capture resolves (CDX-confirmed 200, memento-datetime 2012-07-22) and url_verifier ConnectionErrors on this 7.7MB PDF (a tool timeout, not a liveness fact) -- downloaded directly via curl (200) and ran `pdftotext -layout -f 78 -l 79` manually: Table 4.10 'Gas pipelines in OPEC Members, 2011', Libya section (printed p.75-76), contains the exact row 'Tripoli/Mellitah  Sirte Oil  98  34  16,992,353  na', i.e. OPEC's own statistical bulletin lists this as extant, in-service transport infrastructure in 2011. Independently, the World Bank/Tractebel 2017-18 'Fuel Availability & Opportunities for Cost Reduction' report (downloaded + pdftotext'd; naive substring screen misses place-names in the raw PDF text stream, confirmed manually, same known gotcha as sibling P0483/P1863 shards) describes 'From Mellitah to Tripoli and then to Khoms (222 km) with a nominal capacity of around 600 mmscf/d' as one of the two active trenches of the western Coastal Pipeline section, i.e. an operating, gas-carrying line linking Mellitah and Tripoli as of the report's 2017-18 vintage. Two independent origins (OPEC statistical body, World Bank/Tractebel consultancy), six years apart, agree gas moves between Mellitah and Tripoli on this system; no source found suggesting this specific link is shelved/cancelled. (Context, not cited: a 28 Jul 2026 Xinhua wire on protesters storming the Mellitah complex confirms Mellitah continues to supply gas to local west-Libya power plants right up to that disruption -- consistent with, but not segment-specific to, this line.)

Recovered Wayback ASB2012 Table 4.10 (pdftotext-confirmed, see Status notes) lists 'Tripoli/Mellitah' specifically within the 'Gas pipelines in OPEC Members, 2011' table (as opposed to Table 4.11, the parallel petroleum-product-pipeline table), so Fuel=Gas is definitional to which table the row appears in. World Bank/Tractebel report independently and repeatedly describes the Mellitah-Tripoli-Khoms link as part of the natural-gas '34" Coastal Pipeline system' throughout the document. Two independent origins converge on gas.

Recovered Wayback ASB2012 Table 4.10, Libya, row 'Tripoli/Mellitah | Sirte Oil': Capacity column = 16,992,353 (units: 1,000 scm/yr per the table header) = 16,992,353,000 scm/yr = 16.992353 bcm/y -- an exact match (to 4 significant figures) of the sheet's recorded value (16.99 bcm/y), strong evidence this OPEC row is the sheet's original source datapoint. FLAG (two vintages of a same-named corridor): ognnews.com's project report and the seed Al Wasat (alwasatnews.com) article both describe a materially different, LATER 'Melitah-Tripoli'/'Tripoli-Mellitah' pipeline -- a ~120km NEW-CONSTRUCTION project (per ognnews, ~2005 retender) contracted in 2006 to Punj Lloyd/Joannou & Paraskevaides for Sirte Oil, rated at 200 MMcf/d (~2.07 bcm/y) to supply the Zawiya power station -- an order of magnitude below the sheet's 16.99 bcm/y. The sheet's exact 16.99/158/34 triple matches only the older OPEC-listed Sirte Oil line, not this newer completion project; treated as two distinct historical builds of a same-named corridor (same pattern already flagged on sibling P1864/Khoms-Tripoli) rather than a contradiction to resolve. No second independent source gives this segment's exact capacity; tier medium.

Recovered Wayback ASB2012 Table 4.10, 'Tripoli/Mellitah' row: Length = 98 (the table's 'miles' column header, correctly applied here unlike the sibling Brega/Khoms row) = 98 x 1.609344 = 157.72 km, rounding to the sheet's LengthKnown=158.00 km almost exactly. VALUE DISCREPANCY TO FLAG (redundancy-relevant): the World Bank/Tractebel report gives 222 km for the COMBINED 'Mellitah to Tripoli and then to Khoms' run -- i.e. it treats Mellitah-Tripoli and Tripoli-Khoms as ONE physical trench, not two. Summing the sheet's two separately-recorded segments for this same physical stretch (this row's 158.00 km + sibling P1864 Khoms-Tripoli's 201.00 km = 359 km) is 137 km (62%) MORE than the World Bank/Tractebel figure for the identical Mellitah<->Khoms run. This is the central piece of redundancy evidence -- see the __REDUNDANCY__ resolution below. No second independent source gives this segment's exact standalone length; the ognnews/Al Wasat newer-project sources give ~120 km for their (different-vintage) Melitah-Tripoli project, also not a match. Tier medium (one strong, exact-matching source; a genuine competing measurement exists but is for a different vintage/scope, not treated as invalidating this one).

Recovered Wayback ASB2012 Table 4.10 lists diameter=34 inches for the 'Tripoli/Mellitah | Sirte Oil' row -- exact match. Independently, ognnews.com's project report on the (separate, newer, ~2005-2006-era) Melitah-Tripoli/Khoms-Tripoli completion package specifies '97 kilometres of 34-inch-diameter pipeline, 21 kilometres of 24-inch-diameter pipeline' for the combined works -- the 34in figure recurs across both the older operating line (this row's likely source) and the newer completion project, so both sources agree on 34in even though they otherwise describe different-vintage builds with different lengths/capacities (see Capacity/Length notes).

OPEC ASB2012 Table 4.10 names 'Tripoli/Mellitah' directly under the Libya section, matching StartLocation=Tripoli/EndLocation=Mellitah. Mellitah Oil & Gas's own site (mellitahog.ly, verified live, contains 'Zwara') independently confirms the Mellitah Complex sits in Nuqat al Khams district near Zuwara, supporting EndState/Province='Mellitah' (Nuqat al Khams). Wikipedia's Tripoli article (verified live) independently confirms Tripoli as Libya's capital and Tripoli District. Both endpoints are uncontested, well-documented locations across three independent origins.

OPEC ASB2012 Table 4.10 lists 'Sirte Oil' as owner/operator of the 'Tripoli/Mellitah' row. Wikipedia's Sirte Oil Company article (verified live) independently states SOC is an oil and gas company 'operating under the state-owned National Oil Corporation (NOC)'. NOC's own official affiliated-companies page (noc.ly, verified live, contains 'Sirte') independently lists Sirte Oil and Gas Production and Manufacturing Company among its subsidiaries. Three independent origins (OPEC, Wikipedia, NOC itself) triangulate on NOC/state ownership operating through Sirte Oil, consistent with Owner1=Libyan National Oil Corp. Tier medium rather than high because none of the three sources states the literal 100% ownership figure verbatim -- it is inferred from the absence of any documented JV partner for Sirte Oil Company, matching the treatment already applied to sibling segments P1862/P1863/P1864 in this batch.

Evidence supports a genuine double-count risk, though it does not resolve cleanly to 'yes, definitely redundant' vs 'no.' (1) P1862 Brega-Benghazi (396km) + P1863 Brega-Khoms (645km) + P1864 Khoms-Tripoli (201km) + this row P1865 Tripoli-Mellitah (158km) sum to exactly 1,400 km, retracing the identical Mellitah<->Benghazi coastal corridor that P0483 'Libya Coastal Gas Pipeline' also covers end-to-end as a single aggregate row (1,164 km). Both the 4-segment set and P0483 trace back to overlapping citations: the recovered OPEC ASB2012 Table 4.10 (which lists ONLY the 4 discrete Sirte-Oil-operated segments -- Brega/Benghazi, Brega/Khoms, Khoms/Tripoli, Tripoli/Mellitah -- with no aggregate 'Coastal Pipeline' total line of its own) and the World Bank/Tractebel 2017-18 report (which P0483's shard also used, and which this shard used independently). (2) The two source families do NOT even agree on how many physical trenches make up the western half: OPEC's table (and hence GEM's P1864/P1865 split) treats Khoms-Tripoli and Tripoli-Mellitah as two separate accounting segments (359 km combined), while the World Bank/Tractebel engineering report models the identical Mellitah<->Khoms run as ONE trench of only 222 km -- a 137 km (62%) gap that cannot be explained by rounding or unit error. This suggests OPEC's per-segment table may reflect tariff/ownership accounting boundaries (each stretch separately reported by Sirte Oil) rather than necessarily four separately-built physical pipelines, and raises the possibility the Tripoli split point is not a real physical joint recognized in independent engineering literature. (3) Separately, at least one LATER, smaller-spec 'Melitah-Tripoli'/'Tripoli-Mellitah' pipeline was built/completed circa 2005-2006 (ognnews.com project report; Al Wasat News 2006, Punj Lloyd contract, ~120 km, 200 MMcf/d, built to supply Zawiya power station) -- a different physical asset from the OPEC-table line this row's exact values (158km/34in/16.99 bcm/y) match, adding a further identification wrinkle but not itself evidence of double-counting against P0483. Net read: strong circumstantial evidence that P0483 (aggregate) and the P1862-P1865 segment set describe the SAME underlying physical corridor from overlapping sourcing, with an unreconciled ~20% total-length gap (1,400 km segment-sum vs 1,164 km aggregate) and an internally inconsistent western-half segmentation (OPEC's 2-segment Khoms-Tripoli/Tripoli-Mellitah split vs World Bank/Tractebel's single Mellitah-Khoms trench). This is a candidate for human review to decide whether P0483 should be retired/merged now that the more granular segment rows exist, or whether the segment set should itself be re-consolidated (e.g. merging P1864+P1865 into one Khoms-Mellitah row) to match the independent engineering source's trench boundaries -- not something this researcher can resolve unilaterally without fabricating a reconciliation.
